title: Busting the Myth of Leadership Expertise
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece takes aim at the pervasive myth that effective leaders must always have an answer ready, arguing that the pressure to appear all-knowing actually undermines the credibility it's meant to protect. It walks through why the myth persists (repetition makes ideas feel like fact) and what it costs in practice: leaders faking expertise close off the very conversations that would produce better answers. The counter-model offered is a leader comfortable saying "I don't know, but I'll find out," which the piece frames as building deeper respect rather than eroding authority. The underlying claim is that vulnerability and humility, not omniscience, are what people actually want to follow.
points: The myth that leaders must always have an answer is self-reinforcing through repetition, not because it's empirically true.
Feigning expertise erodes credibility over time even though it's meant to project competence in the moment.
Admitting "I don't know, but I'll find out" opens the door to other perspectives and earns deeper respect than false certainty does.
People follow genuine confidence built on vulnerability and humility, not leaders who project false omniscience.
quotes: Despite empirical evidence to the contrary, once a myth becomes well accepted, it is hard to shake it off.
Among the bag full of leadership myths that have wormed their way into the practice of leadership, perhaps none is more harmful than the accepted dogma that leaders should have all of the answers.
Yet, due to the myth of being all-knowing, leaders are conditioned to have an answer or an opinion to just about any inquiry.
Not having an answer creates the chance for other views, opinions, and answers.
The myth of, “I’m the leader. I should have an answer,” does more to destroy a leader’s credibility than most other falsehoods.
They understand that others most want to follow true confidence, where vulnerability, humility, and open-mindedness express themselves naturally.
